Wednesday 25 November 2026 · 23 stories
Morning Brief
Nifty 50 fell 1.75% to 25,350 with broad selling, 1,858 decliners to 706 advancers
Today’s read
The broader market did better than the busiest names. The median stock moved -1.04% against -2.16% for the fifty most traded stocks, a gap of 1.1 percentage points. Participation was wide.

Shalimar Paints Limited rose 6.7% on 87 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about fund raising, “Allotment of 51948051 securities pursuant to Qualified Institution Placement at its meeting held on November 20, 2026”.

Ajmera Realty & Infra India Limited rose 8.9% on 85 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Premium demand, solid pipeline to spur residential realty growth: Brokerage”.

The exchange has formally asked 2 companies to explain today's move: Windsor Machines Limited, ITI Limited. Those queries were filed after the close, so they confirm the move rather than explain it. NSE's own surveillance flagged the same names.

Nothing in the news or in exchange filings explains the volume in ITI Limited (310x), Ugro Capital Limited (173x), HMA Agro Industries Limited (78x). That usually points to a sector story rather than a company one.

Top defence stocks to buy: Apollo Micro Systems, BEL, Data Patterns, GRSE, Zen Technologies - check Choice's top picks
Choice Institutional Equities initiated coverage with Buy ratings on seven Indian defence companies, citing expanding order books and domestic procurement mandates. High price-to-earnings valuations across the sector leave little margin for revenue execution delays at Bharat Electronics and Data Patterns. Monthly ministry of defence contract announcements will confirm if order inflow momentum matches these earnings projections.

US planning to hike tariffs against India, 15 other countries: Report - The Tribune
The United States is considering higher import tariffs on 16 countries, including India, according to trade reports. Higher tariffs directly threaten Indian merchandise export volumes, squeezing operating margins for listed exporters in the textile, auto component, and pharmaceutical sectors. The official release of the US tariff schedule will confirm specific product categories and duty rates.
Geopolitics
IIFCL IPO: Govt plans to sell part of its stake, company to issue fresh shares
The government plans an initial public offering for India Infrastructure Finance Company by the end of this fiscal year through an offer for sale and fresh equity issue. The fresh capital will expand IIFCL's lending capacity for core infrastructure projects, intensifying competition for non-banking financial companies like REC and PFC. Third-quarter asset quality metrics will confirm its post-listing loan growth capacity.

Shalimar Paints to merge with promoter Infra.Market in Rs 19,839-crore deal; Tiger Global, Accel, Nexus...
Shalimar Paints will merge into its promoter entity, Infra.Market, in a transaction valuing the combined business at 19,839 crore rupees. The merger provides Shalimar access to Infra.Market's nationwide building materials distribution channel while offering institutional backers an exit path. The appointed valuation report and share swap ratio will clarify equity dilution for minority shareholders.

India and Netherlands looking at boosting cooperation in clean energy, shipbuilding: MEA
India and the Netherlands agreed to expand cooperation in green hydrogen and shipbuilding following bilateral talks in New Delhi. This high-level diplomatic agreement creates no immediate financial impact for listed Indian shipbuilders or energy companies. Concrete commercial contracts or port infrastructure concessions will indicate whether listed firms benefit from this partnership.

Next quarter's discretionary technology spending commentary from US clients will confirm whether foreign selling persists.

US stocks slide as Nvidia rally fizzles out, dollar falls
US equities ended lower as Nvidia reversed intraday gains, while the US dollar index softened. A weaker greenback helps stabilize the Indian rupee and reduces import costs for crude oil. However, valuation pressure on US megacap tech typically dampens investor appetite for Indian IT exporters like Infosys and TCS.

Can Amazon’s Trainium chips reduce its dependence on Nvidia? The Decart technology acquisition offers clues
Amazon acquired AI startup Decart to enhance software performance on its proprietary Trainium chips, bypassing Nvidia hardware. Cheaper custom chips lower cloud compute costs for enterprises, accelerating deployment budgets. This expands contract opportunities for Indian IT services firms like LTIMindtree and Persistent Systems that build enterprise AI integration software.

High valuations and persistent foreign portfolio outflows continue to weigh on private lenders like ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank. Explained: Why Gold prices gained and extended a rebound from a 14-month low - 3 reasons

Rising bullion prices increase underlying asset values and lower credit risk for gold loan NBFCs like Muthoot Finance. Conversely, elevated prices typically compress near-term retail volume growth for jewelers like Titan Company.

Asian markets fell, led by a 3.7% slump in South Korea's Kospi, as doubts over tech earnings valuation reappeared. A broader regional risk-off environment accelerates net foreign portfolio equity outflows from India. This places downside pressure on liquid large-cap counters in the Nifty 50 index.

Chalet Hotels: is the worst behind it?
Chalet Hotels announced an ambitious expansion plan targeting room additions through FY31, even as near-term revenue per available room faces margin pressure from elevated debt and execution delays. The heavy capital expenditure cycle will suppress return on equity and free cash flows across hospitality peers in the medium term. Monthly RevPAR data and occupancy rates will indicate whether pricing power can offset rising borrowing costs.
Mint Markets
AI boom looms over Warsh's Fed as inflation worries grow
Former Fed Governor Kevin Warsh warned that massive capital spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure could sustain short-term inflationary pressure before delivering productivity gains. Persistent US inflation raises the risk of prolonged elevated Fed policy rates, driving higher US Treasury yields and strengthening the dollar. This scenario typically restricts foreign portfolio inflows into Indian emerging market equities and pressures the rupee.

US President praises India’s economic growth & low interest rates - News On AIR
Political remarks praising Indian economic growth and low interest rates provide no new policy shifts or material data for fundamental investors.
Fed and rates
Fed faces a dangerous inflation dilemma as recession fears grow - TheStreet
The US Federal Reserve faces dual risks of sticky service inflation and slowing economic growth, complicating its monetary easing trajectory. Prolonged US economic deceleration weakens export demand for Indian IT services, pharmaceuticals, and auto components while keeping global risk sentiment volatile. Upcoming US Personal Consumption Expenditures price index data will confirm whether the Fed can continue cutting rates.

Companies and earnings
Valuation, debt worries overshadow Tata Steel-APL Apollo deal’s strategic gains
Shares of Tata Steel and APL Apollo Tubes dropped after transaction details showed a delay of over three years before downstream capacity additions yield earnings accretion. The extended gestation period adds debt-servicing burdens and depresses return on invested capital, overshadowing long-term volume gains for both steelmakers. Quarterly debt metrics and downstream volume execution over the next two quarters will clarify margin realization timelines.
Mint Markets
Japan Stocks’ Rebound Threatened as Retail Margin Losses Balloon
Japanese retail margin traders hold expanding margin losses after recent market volatility, threatening forced liquidations. Margin calls in Tokyo routinely spur cross-border unwinds, driving foreign institutional investors to withdraw funds from emerging markets like India to meet domestic cash requirements. A sustained appreciation of the yen against the dollar will signal whether forced selling spreads to Indian equities.
Mint Markets
Investors, proxy firms question fairness of APL Apollo's ₹28k-cr Tata Steel deal
Proxy advisory firms raised governance concerns over APL Apollo Tubes funding a 28,000 crore rupee asset purchase from Tata Steel via debt, while Tata Steel spends 15,510 crore rupees for a 26.38 percent promoter stake. Higher leverage and execution risk threaten to contract APL Apollo valuation multiples. Conversely, Tata Steel secures balance sheet deleveraging. Shareholders vote on the transaction next month.
Mint Companies
HDFC Bank, Kotak, Axis need faster retail deposit growth for share re-rating: Jefferies
Jefferies highlighted that retail deposit growth at HDFC Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, and Axis Bank continues to lag regional peers. Slower low-cost deposit accumulation forces these lenders to rely on expensive bulk funding, pressing net interest margins down and constraining loan expansion. This trend prevents price-to-book valuation re-ratings across large-cap banking stocks. Monthly deposit growth figures will confirm if margin pressures persist.

US Tariff Alert: Why Trump is planning fresh import duties on India, China and other nations: Reports - News24Online
Reports indicate the incoming US administration plans fresh import duties on goods from India and China. Higher tariffs directly threaten Indian export-oriented sectors, particularly textiles, auto components, and generic pharmaceuticals, by reducing price competitiveness in the American market. The policy shifts risk widening India current account deficit and pressuring the rupee. Official US Trade Representative policy statements will confirm the targeted tariff rates.
Geopolitics
India, China, over two dozen other nations face higher US tariffs over industrial subsidies: Report - WION
The United States is preparing targeted tariff hikes against India and two dozen other nations, citing unfair state industrial subsidies. Securing export market share becomes harder for Indian engineering exporters and chemical manufacturers facing potential countervailing duties. This regulatory shift threatens export earnings and operating margins for mid-cap capital goods companies. Monthly commerce ministry trade data will show early impacts on outbound shipments.
Geopolitics
US Plans To Raise Tariffs On India, China And Other Major Trading Partners: Report - News18
Proposed US tariff hikes targeting India and major trading partners threaten global trade volumes and Indian export revenue. A broader trade conflict weakens foreign portfolio inflows into domestic equities while exerting depreciating pressure on the rupee against the dollar. The move particularly impacts price realization for steel, aluminum, and manufacturing exporters. Foreign institutional flow data over coming weeks will measure foreign investor response.
